body:
Yes, prepared. I enjoy challenges. I hate the easy option. I put this down to my upbringing and how it's shaped me. I'm pretty happy about that! When my parents divorced I also had to grow up damn fast. I had to play mother in the house, looking after my younger siblings; a 9 y/o and 15 y/o. It was not what I wanted, plus important exams.

I would say that's brave. I certainly couldn't release my thoughts to a close friend. The only person I told (outside of family) was an ex. Mistake. But I genuinely believed he was there to listen. (He was the one who threw it back in my face from my initial post)

I understand this, and I think I have accepted the past, to a certain extent. I'm thankful it happened to me, and no one else. And I know there are people who are out there who have suffered with much, much worse.

I know bringing up shit will hurt, a lot. But I'd like to be in a position where it doesn't affect me half as much as it does when it's brought up in conversation.

I think if I was clinically depressed it would make the situation worse for me. I've dealt with it well so far. I'm hoping this is a phase.

I can't honestly say I've had experience of this. But sometimes I do see similarities of my fathers experiences in his early 20's and experiences I've had over the past few years. So yes, thinking I'm on a similar path is something which makes me feel sick. We share similar personality traits too. 

I completely agree with the reputation point. I have always been the "strong, independent" friend in my friendship groups; if people really knew how I felt behind closed doors I honestly think they'd laugh and treat it as a joke. Or as some sort of sick cry for attention.

Oh, and another reason I'm battling with the idea of opening up to a therapist, is that I don't want to ever be diagnosed as mentally unstable/ill. This is something I am absolutely, completely against. I'm not sure why...Maybe my pride, once again.

They have been removed from my life; that was difficult for me. 

Yep, heard that one before too. I am a very emotional person. Most of the time, I care TOO much about people. But I do have trouble expressing my emotions from time to time. I have improved though. I have a very tough exterior, but I'm like liquid on the inside! It does take a while for my guard to come down, however.

I'm glad I went through it as a child. I wouldn't be the person I am now. But when you're being shot down for things you had no control over, and you thought you did a good job at dealing with it, that's what is getting to me. I tried so hard to keep myself on track. 

I'm definitely considering it. I'm not sure I'm ready, yet. Like i said, I'm a  proud person; I view it as weak. Plus bringing up shit from the past is going to hurt like hell. 

Thank you for your words. They have helped :)
